title: Services

header.html: Provide and troubleshoot access to applications via services

toc.title: Names, DNS and reaching a Service

html:
1Why a Service

Pods come and go, and each new Pod has a new IP address. A Service is a stable virtual IP and DNS name in front of a set of Pods. It picks the Pods with a label selector and spreads connections across the ones that are Ready. The list of Ready Pod addresses is kept in EndpointSlices (k get endpoints <svc> still shows the classic view).

Service type Reachable from Use it for
ClusterIP (default) inside the cluster only internal communication between apps
NodePort <any node IP>:<nodePort> (30000 to 32767) and inside simple external access, tests
LoadBalancer an external IP from a cloud load balancer, plus a NodePort and ClusterIP production access on a cloud (here the address stays pending)
ExternalName inside the cluster; returns a DNS CNAME a stable in-cluster name for an outside host
headless (clusterIP: None) DNS returns the Pod IPs directly StatefulSets, client-side load balancing

2Create a Service

k expose deployment shop --port=8080 --target-port=80                 # ClusterIP, name shop
k expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort      # NodePort (random node port)
k expose pod web --port=80                                           # for a Pod
k create service clusterip db --tcp=5432:5432                        # selector app=db
k create service externalname legacy-db --external-name=db.example.com

expose copies the selector from the Deployment's Pod labels, so it is the safest way. To fix a node port, generate YAML and add nodePort: 30080 to the port.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop}
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector: {app: shop}            # must match the Pod labels
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 8080                     # the Service's own port
    targetPort: 80                 # the container port (a number or a port NAME)
    protocol: TCP
Field Meaning
port the port clients use on the Service
targetPort the port on the Pod (default: same as port); may be the name of a containerPort
nodePort the fixed port on every node, NodePort and LoadBalancer only
selector labels of the Pods to serve; a Service without a selector has no automatic endpoints

Several ports: each port needs a unique name. Named target ports (targetPort: http) let the container port number change without touching the Service.

3Names, DNS and reaching a Service

Cluster DNS (CoreDNS) gives every Service a name:

Name Works from
shop a Pod in the same namespace
shop.svc1 any namespace
shop.svc1.svc.cluster.local everywhere (the full name)

Test from a throw-away Pod: k run tmp --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 http://shop.svc1:8080. Environment variables SHOP_SERVICE_HOST and SHOP_SERVICE_PORT also appear in Pods created after the Service (the DNS name is the better habit).

From your own terminal, reach a Service or Pod without exposing it: k port-forward svc/shop 8080:8080 (then curl localhost:8080 in another terminal), or k port-forward pod/web 8080:80.

4Troubleshoot a Service

Work from the inside out. These are the classic causes, in the order of how often they appear on the exam:

Check Command Typical finding
Does the Service have endpoints? k get endpoints shop (or k get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=shop) <none>: the selector matches no Ready Pod
Do the selector and the Pod labels match? k get svc shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}' and k get pods --show-labels a typo, or the Service says app=web and the Pods say app=webapp
Are the Pods Ready? k get pods 0/1 Ready (readiness probe failing) keeps them out of the endpoints
Is targetPort the port the app listens on? k get svc shop -o yaml, k describe pod connection refused: wrong targetPort
Is the name resolving? k exec <pod> -- nslookup shop wrong namespace in the name
Is a NetworkPolicy blocking? k get netpol Module 16
Right namespace? -n <ns> the Service lives in another namespace 
k get svc,endpoints -n svc3
k describe svc api -n svc3          # Selector, Port, TargetPort, Endpoints
k patch svc api -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'

A Service whose selector matches nothing "hangs" (no endpoints, packets go nowhere); a wrong targetPort is refused ("connection refused"). Fix the Service, unless the task says to fix the Pods' labels.

Exam tip

. k describe svc <name> shows the Endpoints line. Empty endpoints mean a selector or readiness problem; filled endpoints but no answer mean a port problem.

Exam tip

. "Expose the Deployment on port X" is k expose deployment <name> --port=X --target-port=<container port>. Check the Deployment's container port, not just its image.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m14 -->

Lab 14.1: clusterip service

Domain: Networking | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-01-clusterip-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc1, the Deployment shop (2 replicas, nginx:alpine, listening on port 80) exists. Create a Service named shop of type ClusterIP that is reachable inside the cluster on port 8080 and forwards to the containers' port 80.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc1 expose deployment shop --port=8080 --target-port=80
kubectl -n svc1 get svc shop

Lab 14.2: nodeport service

Domain: Networking | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-02-nodeport-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc2, expose the Deployment web (nginx on port 80) with a Service named web-np of type NodePort, service port 80, using the fixed node port 30080.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc2 expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web-np.yaml
sed -i 's/  - port: 80/  - port: 80\n    nodePort: 30080/' /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 apply -f /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 get svc web-np

Lab 14.3: fix service selector

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-03-fix-service-selector)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc3, the Service api does not work: requests to http://api.svc3 hang. The Deployment api (2 replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that http://api.svc3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc3 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=api
kubectl -n svc3 get svc api -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n svc3 get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n svc3 patch svc api -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'

Lab 14.4: endpoint ips

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-04-endpoint-ips)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc4, the Service db is backed by several Pods. Write the IP addresses of all Pods that currently serve the Service (one IP per line, sorted) to ~/answers/endpoints.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db
kubectl -n svc4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].endpoints[*]}{.addresses[0]}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/endpoints.txt

Lab 14.5: loadbalancer service

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-05-loadbalancer-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc5, expose the Deployment front (nginx, port 80) with a Service named front-lb of type LoadBalancer on port 80. In this test cluster there is no cloud load balancer, so the external address stays pending; only the Service definition is checked.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc5 expose deployment front --name=front-lb --port=80 --type=LoadBalancer
kubectl -n svc5 get svc front-lb

Lab 14.6: externalname

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-06-externalname)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc6, create a Service named legacy-db that makes the name legacy-db.svc6.svc.cluster.local resolve (as a DNS alias) to the external host db.example.com.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc6 create service externalname legacy-db --external-name=db.example.com
kubectl -n svc6 get svc legacy-db

Lab 14.7: cross namespace dns

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-07-cross-namespace-dns)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod server (nginx) runs in the namespace back and the Pod client (busybox) runs in the namespace front. Make the client able to fetch the nginx page from the server by the name http://server.back (do not touch the Pods). Then write the full DNS name of the Service (including .svc.cluster.local) to ~/answers/fqdn.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n back expose pod server --port=80
kubectl -n front exec client -- wget -qO- -T3 http://server.back | head -3
echo server.back.svc.cluster.local > ~/answers/fqdn.txt

Lab 14.8: multiport service

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-08-multiport-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc8, the Deployment app (2 replicas) has Pods that listen on port 80 (web) and 8080 (metrics; the image is nginx so only 80 answers, the definition is what counts). Create a Service named app that exposes two named ports: http on port 80 targeting container port 80, and metrics on port 9090 targeting container port 8080.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc8 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: app}
spec:
  selector: {app: app}
  ports:
  - {name: http, port: 80, targetPort: 80}
  - {name: metrics, port: 9090, targetPort: 8080}
Y
kubectl -n svc8 get svc app

Lab 14.9: fix target port

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m14-09-fix-target-port)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc9, requests to http://site.svc9 fail with "connection refused". The Deployment site (2 replicas of nginx:alpine, which listens on port 80) is healthy and the Service site selects its Pods correctly. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that http://site.svc9 returns the nginx welcome page.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc9 get endpoints site
kubectl -n svc9 get svc site -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0]}'; echo
kubectl -n svc9 patch service site --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":80}]'
probe http://site.svc9 svc9 | head -3

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1What decides which Pods a Service sends traffic to?

Show the answer

Its label selector, and only Pods that are Ready.

R2What is the difference between port, targetPort and nodePort?

Show the answer

port is the Service's port, targetPort is the Pod's port, nodePort is the fixed port on every node (NodePort and LoadBalancer).

R3What range do node ports use?

Show the answer

30000 to 32767 by default.

R4What is the full DNS name of Service shop in namespace svc1?

Show the answer

shop.svc1.svc.cluster.local.

R5What does empty ENDPOINTS for a Service mean?

Show the answer

No Ready Pod matches the selector: check labels and readiness.

R6What does an ExternalName Service return?

Show the answer

A DNS CNAME to the external host name; it has no selector and no proxying.

R7How do you reach a Service from your terminal without exposing it?

Show the answer

kubectl port-forward svc/<name> <local>:<port>.

R8What is a headless Service?

Show the answer

A Service with clusterIP: None: DNS returns the Pod IPs, not one virtual IP.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Types ClusterIP, NodePort (30000-32767), LoadBalancer, ExternalName, headless
Create k expose deployment x --port --target-port [--type]
Ports port (Service), targetPort (Pod, number or name), nodePort
DNS svc, svc.ns, svc.ns.svc.cluster.local
Endpoints selector must match Ready Pods; get endpoints, describe svc
Debug selector vs labels, readiness, targetPort, namespace, NetworkPolicy
Local test port-forward, a throw-away busybox Pod with wget
